caption: The video captures a stone-clad fireplace behind a metal mesh screen, set on a stone hearth above a wooden floor. A metal rack stands against the left wall, a dark storage box rests on the right side of the hearth, and a patterned rug edge shows at the bottom left. Inside the firebox, a pile of logs burns with a large, bright yellow-white flame that fills the upper cavity. A paperback book stands upright at the center base of the firebox, positioned directly in front of the flames. Throughout the excerpt the fire flickers continuously, the shape, height, and brightness of the flame tongues shifting from frame to frame. The white glow at the top pulses, while the flames on either side of the log pile rise and recede. Despite this restless movement of the fire, the logs, the standing book, the screen, and the surrounding objects remain fixed in place. The camera framing stays essentially static, so the only visible change is confined to the burning fire itself. The flames keep flickering across the whole clip, with no new object entering and none of the fixed elements moving.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
